import pytz

# Define the failure time window in UTC+8 timezone
tz = pytz.timezone('Asia/Shanghai')
start_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-04-11 02:00:00', tz=tz)
end_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-04-11 02:30:00', tz=tz)

# Convert metric_df timestamp to datetime with timezone
metric_df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(metric_df['timestamp'], unit='s').dt.tz_localize('UTC').dt.tz_convert(tz)

# Define possible root cause components
node_components = [f'os_{str(i).zfill(3)}' for i in range(1, 23)]
container_components = [f'docker_{str(i).zfill(3)}' for i in range(1, 9)]
service_components = [f'db_{str(i).zfill(3)}' for i in range(1, 14)]

# Filter metrics for these components
root_cause_components = node_components + container_components + service_components
root_metrics = metric_df[metric_df['cmdb_id'].isin(root_cause_components)].copy()

# Calculate global P95 thresholds for each component-KPI using entire data
thresholds = root_metrics.groupby(['cmdb_id', 'name'])['value'].quantile(0.95).reset_index()
thresholds.rename(columns={'value': 'p95_threshold'}, inplace=True)

# Filter time series data within the failure time window

# We keep the timestamp and value for anomaly detection

# Display the thresholds and a sample of the aggregated time series for verification
